summary: Kapila Vatsyayan was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at Delhi and BHU, and held leadership roles at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (1987-2005) and India International Centre (~2005-2012).

Karel Werner was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Masaryk University and under Robert Konečný, Jaroslav Průšek, and Vincenc Lesný at Palacký University. He taught at Palacký (~1949-1964), Durham (1969-1990), and Masaryk University (1993-1998).

Karen Cheatham is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a master's degree from the Graduate Theological Union and a doctoral degree from the University of Toronto (attested 2007).

Karen Christina Lang is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg and Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, later serving as professor at Virginia.

Karen L. Brock is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. from Princeton University. She served as an assistant professor at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1988) and at the University of Michigan (attested 1990).

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942-2015) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University. She held a post at Temple (~1971-1976) and served as professor of anthropology at Drew University (~1976-2009).

Karen Nelson Villanueva is a religious studies scholar. She completed her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2013) and studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (~2000-2008) and the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she worked as a senior teaching fellow, before lecturing at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020).

Karin Meyers works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and held a post at Kathmandu University as an assistant professor and director of the MA program in Buddhist studies at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz is an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held positions at the Free University of Berlin, the University of British Columbia, and the University of Vienna (from 1999).

Karl Ammer (1911-1970) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Vienna (~1930-1934). He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1955-1968) and directed the Institute of Indology at the University of Halle (~1957-1968).

Karl Benedikt Hase (1780-1864) was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the universities of Jena and Helmstedt. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1805-1864), École des langues orientales (1816-1864), and the Faculty of Arts of Paris (1852-1864).

Karl Brugmann (1849-1919) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Georg Curtius at Halle and Leipzig. He was a professor at the University of Freiburg (1884) and held a chair in Indo-European linguistics at Leipzig University (1887-1919).

Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under several traditional teachers, including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Wu Hung and Jennifer Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal (1812-1894) was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, where he later held an academic post from approximately 1842 to 1845.
Karl Eugen Neumann (1865-1915) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig University (~1887-1888) and completed doctoral studies under Richard Pischel (~1888-1891).
Karl Felix Halm (1809-1882) was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar. He held concurrent posts at the University of Munich (~1856-1882) and the Bavarian State Library (~1856-1882).

Karl Ferdinand Johansson (1860-1926) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Uppsala University in 1880 and later served there as University Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology of Indo-European Languages from approximately 1893 to 1925.
